thread.title: Nikkei lags, but other Asian markets gain to open November

author: morningstar.com
title: Nikkei lags, but other Asian markets gain to open November
text:
By Dow Jones Newswires
Telecom stocks dive in Japan; Chinese stocks surge
After a roller-coaster October, Asian stock markets started November with widespread gains.
Japan was the notable exception, with the Nikkei down 0.5% amid caution over U.S. trade policies and the upcoming midterm elections. The telecom sector fell 6.3%, by far the worst among 33 Topix sectors, after NTT DoCoMo said it would cut mobile service charges. NTT DoCoMo (9437.TO) was down 11% while fellow telecom KDDI (9433.TO) dropped 15% and SoftBank Group (9984.TO) sank 6.9%. Panasonic (6752.TO) was also sharply down.
Meanwhile, Chinese stocks surged Thursday, with Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index jumping 1.4%. Apple Inc. (AAPL) suppliers Sunny Optical (2382.HK) and AAC Tech (2018.HK) , rose 3.6% and 3.8%, respectively, a day after Apple unveiled new computers and iPads. Country Garden (2007.HK) and China Overseas Land (0688.HK) rose 8.2% and 3.2%, respectively, after what UOB Kay Hian analyst Ivan Ip called an upbeat assessment on mainland China's construction recovery from yesterday's PMI reading. Among the losers, CLP Holdings (0002.HK) was down 1.3% and Power Assets (0006.HK) slipped 1.1%.
Mainland China benchmarks continued higher, as the latest Politburo meeting called for "healthy development" of the capital market, with Shanghai Composite gaining 1.1%. The smaller-cap Shenzhen Composite was up 1.5%, following its seventh straight monthly decline. Some AI-related names popped, boosted by President Xi Jinping's pep talk, while infrastructure stocks outperformed the boarder market.
Australia's ASX 200 rose 0.3%, as BHP Billiton (BHP.AU) rose after announcing a plan to give $10.4 billion from its shale sale to investors via an equally split buyback and special dividend. Stocks in New Zealand rose as well.
Taiwan's Taiex gained 0.5% despite fears that the country's economic slowdown could be worse than it seems, after third-quarter GDP grew 2.28% year-over-year, slower than the previous quarter's 3.3% expansion. Benchmark indexes in South Korea , Singapore and Malaysia all posted solid gains.
-Dow Jones Newswires;
